# Huma

> Huma is a free writing app, on the web and on Mac, that records how a person types and gives them a link and a PDF Report showing a person wrote the text, not AI. Anyone can open the link in a browser and check it, with no account.

Huma is not an AI detector. AI detectors read finished text and guess; Huma records the writing as it happens, so its proof comes from how the text was made.

Key facts:

- How it works: write in Huma, press Finish, share the link. The proof is made on the writer's own computer in seconds.
- What a reader sees: the text exactly as written (any later change breaks the proof), the Huma Score (how much was typed and how much was pasted), a PDF Report, and, if the writer allows it, a replay of the writing.
- Pasted text is allowed and marked as pasted.
- Who uses it: students flagged by AI detectors, freelance writers, job seekers sending cover letters, newsletter and LinkedIn writers.
- Price: free.
- Accounts: not needed to write; writers sign in at Finish to get a link. Readers never need an account.
- Browsers: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on a computer. The Mac app adds a stronger check: every key press is confirmed from the keyboard.
- Length: up to 10,000 characters per document, about 1,500 words.
- Limits: Huma proves a person typed the text in Huma; it can't tell where the ideas came from, and it covers only what is written in it, not earlier work.

- [Ask for a Huma link](https://huma.social/ask): ask someone to send writing as a Huma link
